newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela aluminum sell-off draws 13 companies.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela aluminum sell-off draws 13 companies.

text.p: The privatization of Venezuela's four-company aluminum sector has drawn 13 interested companies from Canada, the United States, Australia, Switzerland, Norway and Venezuela, leading daily El Nacional reported Thursday.

The companies which have registered for the sale of smelters Alcasa and Venalum, carbon anode producer Carbonorca and bauxite and alumina producer Bauxilum will now be assessed by the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) and investment bank Merrill Lynch.
The list of pre-qualified bidders will be announced on Sept 16 with an eye to selling between 60 and 80 percent stake in the aluminum sector to a sole bidder in mid December.

According to El Nacional, the companies which registered for the sell-off were: Alumax, Aluminum Company of America (Alcoa), Glencore International, Reynolds Metals Co, Kaiser Aluminium Corp, Alentuy/Ormet Corp, Norkhidro, Alcan Aluminium Ltd, Mitsubishi Metals Corp, Cra Ltd, Billington, Sural and Marubeni.
Amalysts say the four companies, which include Venalum's 430,000 tonnes per year capacity smelter, are worth about $2 billion.
